node-1.label: Woman in her 20s presented with well-demarcated hand dermatitis on the left and right third fingers

node-2.label: The dermatitis was recalcitrant and unresponsive to topical medications including corticosteroids

node-3.label: Medical history was remarkable for 'eczema' dating back to childhood; patch testing results were negative

node-4.label: Physical examination showed sharply demarcated erythematous scaly plaques with fissures, scale crust, and nail pitting on the left and right third fingers; the left third finger was confluently covered while the rest of the hand was unaffected

why.why: The skin biopsy demonstrates intraepidermal neutrophil-rich spongiform pustules and nail bed acanthosis with spongiform pustules, which both the pathologist and laboratory physician analyses identify as characteristic/pathognomonic for psoriasis. Combined with the clinical sharply demarcated scaly plaques and nail pitting, this strongly confirms psoriatic dermatitis/psoriasis, raising confidence from 0.65 to 0.95.

The biopsy showing psoriatic histology is not compatible with chronic endogenous eczema, and the sharply demarcated plaques and nail pitting are atypical. Expert analyses state chronic eczema can be clearly excluded, so confidence decreases from 0.15 to 0.03 despite the childhood eczema history.

Negative patch testing already refuted allergic contact dermatitis, and the biopsy reveals psoriasis-specific histology supporting the leading diagnosis rather than an exogenous dermatitis. No exposure evidence supports an exogenous cause, so confidence is reduced from 0.10 to 0.03.

The biopsy showing neutrophil-rich spongiform pustules is characteristic of psoriasis and, according to both expert analyses, effectively excludes fungal infection as the primary process. Sharply demarcated plaques and nail pitting also favor psoriasis, so confidence falls from 0.10 to 0.02 even though KOH/PAS results were not obtained.
